newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-3RD NZ/ENGLAND TEST EVENLY POISED AT LUNCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-3RD NZ/ENGLAND TEST EVENLY POISED AT LUNCH.

text.p: The third and final cricket test match between England and New Zealand was evenly poised at lunch on the first day at Lancaster Park on Friday.
After being sent in to bat, New Zealand were 85 for two at the interval.
New cap Matt Horne had made a good fist of his debut and was on 31, while new captain Stephen Fleming was on two.

The Kiwis, seeking a win to square the three-match series after England won the second test at Wellington to go one up, would have had an excellent morning if not for the loss of opener Blair Pocock 20 minutes before the break.

After Bryan Young had taken 10 runs from Dominic Cork in the first over of the day, he was bowled for 11 in Cork's second over. But Pocock and Horne added 64 for the second wicket in 86 minutes to set the New Zealand innings up.

However, England fought back to leave the scales balanced at lunch when Pocock was out for 22. Pocock tried to slam offspinner Robert Croft over mid on, but miscued and was caught by captain Mike Atherton at a shortish mid on position.
Horne played some handsome drives and got through a lively opening period, which contained several short-pitched deliveries and some verbal advice from Cork.
By lunch he had hit four fours in his 111-minute stay.
Fleming, who at 23 became New Zealand's youngest ever test captain when he was called in to take over from the injured Lee Germon, got through to lunch without mishap.
Cork had taken one for 33 in six wayward overs, while Croft had taken one for 12 in six overs.
